issue.title: mongo-cxx-driver build problem

repository.name: vcpkg
repository.description: C++ Library Manager for Windows, Linux, and MacOS

issue.body:
I got a problem trying to build mongo-cxx-driver static library. While building dependence - mongo-c-driver I've got an output:
CMake Error at scripts/cmake/vcpkg_execute_required_process.cmake:14 (message):
    Command failed: C:/Data/projects/vcpkg/downloads/cmake-3.5.2-win32-x86/bin/cmake.exe;--build;.;--config;Release;--target;install;--;/m
    Working Directory: C:/Data/projects/vcpkg/buildtrees/mongo-c-driver/x64-windows-static-rel
    See logs for more information:
      C:\Data\projects\vcpkg\buildtrees\mongo-c-driver\package-x64-windows-static-rel-out.log
      C:\Data\projects\vcpkg\buildtrees\mongo-c-driver\package-x64-windows-static-rel-err.log

Call Stack (most recent call first):
  scripts/cmake/vcpkg_install_cmake.cmake:3 (vcpkg_execute_required_process)
  ports/mongo-c-driver/portfile.cmake:20 (vcpkg_install_cmake)
  scripts/ports.cmake:73 (include)
Error: building package mongo-c-driver:x64-windows-static failed
Please ensure sure you're using the latest portfiles with `vcpkg update`, then
submit an issue at https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg/issues including:
  Package: mongo-c-driver:x64-windows-static
  Vcpkg version: 0.0.65-b280f57002044036c1c3c9a446c06e8e0a34fb00

The problem is: bson.h: No such file or directory.

I'm using Windows 10, Russian locale.

Update: In the generated projects properties (vcpkg\buildtrees\mongo-c-driver\x64-windows-static-dbg\libmongoc.sln) I saw something like "BSON_INCLUDE_DIR-NOTFOUND" in the include paths. So I added
-DBSON_INCLUDE_DIR=${CURRENT_INSTALLED_DIR}/include
to portfile.cmake next to other options. After I got vcpkg\installed\x64-windows-static\include\libbson-1.0. If I remove libbson-1.0, I can build the library manually via visual studio solution.

issue.title: poco can't find pcre.h

labels.name: category:port-bug
labels.description: The issue is with a library, which is something the port should already support

repository.name: vcpkg
repository.description: C++ Library Manager for Windows, Linux, and MacOS

issue.body:
Package: poco:x64-windows
Vcpkg version: 0.0.71-ce477bf21998c80afc551de72c6140178de3a114

poco is unable to find pcre.h, build fails.
[package-x64-windows-rel-out.txt](https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg/files/752542/package-x64-windows-rel-out.txt)

body:
From #632 (indicating that this still occurs on recent versions):
> Package: poco:x64-windows
Vcpkg version: 0.0.71-ce477bf21998c80afc551de72c6140178de3a114
poco is unable to find pcre.h, build fails.

Ok, I am able to reproduce this locally. Looking further, it seems like POCO _is_ correctly finding PCRE's include directory.
```
// buildtrees\poco\x86-windows-rel\CMakeCache.txt
...
//Path to a file.
PCRE_INCLUDE_DIR:PATH=D:/src/vcpkg/installed/x86-windows/include
...
```
However it isn't actually including it during the JSON component build (the one that fails); only during the Foundation build. This was a "regression" introduced in https://github.com/pocoproject/poco/commit/e863111a2c5aa6bd7d4bd0dc656f81fc26e812ad to fix another issue.

I am now testing a fix which adds `${PCRE_INCLUDE_DIRS}` to the `PUBLIC` section of the Foundation library target inside POCO. This should automatically cause all other targets that depend on Foundation to have the PCRE header path added.
I've uploaded the above fix. Please let me know if this did not solve the issue on your machine!

issue.title: Cannot find 'pcre.h' when using POCO_UNBUNDLED, a non-system PCRE, and CMake

repository.name: poco
repository.description: The POCO C++ Libraries are powerful cross-platform C++ libraries for building network- and internet-based applications that run on desktop, server, mobile, IoT, and embedded systems.

issue.body:
Related to Microsoft/vcpkg#475.

As part of the fix in e863111, a public header dependency was added from Foundation to PCRE. This wasn't reflected in the CMake buildsystem; notably, the JSON component uses RegularExpression from Foundation but does _not_ have `${PCRE_INCLUDE_DIRS}` added to its include paths.

On *nix systems where PCRE is available through `/usr/include`, this will not appear because JSON will implicitly have that directory added to its compile line. However, when using a privately-built version of PCRE, the header will be missing.

In Vcpkg, I've patched this issue via Microsoft/vcpkg@1bfd724 [1], but I don't think that's the optimal upstream fix for POCO. Instead, I believe the clear intention (given the style of `RegularExpression.h`) is to completely hide PCRE as an implementation detail.

Therefore, I believe the best fix would be to completely eliminate all references to the PCRE structs from the header and instead replace the types of `_pcre` and `_extra`[2] with `void*`. In the implementation, these `void*`s would be cast to the correct PCRE structure when used. This would eliminate the header file dependence on the macro `POCO_UNBUNDLED` and completely avoid the problem of forward declaring structures from other libraries.

[1]
```diff
diff --git a/Foundation/CMakeLists.txt b/Foundation/CMakeLists.txt
index 76005b1..efc99b6 100644
--- a/Foundation/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/Foundation/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -166,6 +166,7 @@ target_link_libraries( "${LIBNAME}" ${SYSLIBS})
 target_include_directories( "${LIBNAME}"
 	PUBLIC
 		$<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
+		$<BUILD_INTERFACE:${PCRE_INCLUDE_DIRS}>
 		$<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
 	PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src
 	)
```

[2] https://github.com/pocoproject/poco/blob/develop/Foundation/include/Poco/RegularExpression.h#L217-L218
